# Report - video30, L1 proxy, CineRecon Three.js sampled-frame baseline

Representation level: L1 (simple geometric proxies). Protocol: Three.js sampled-frame baseline with native render-inspect-revise rounds (not a Blender-equivalent reproduction).

## Observed in the 24 reference samples
- Onboard footage from a blue F1 car on a circuit, sunny sky, trees, grandstands, green sponsor boards.
- Shot 1 (samples 0-6, 0.00-2.60 s): low camera above the nose; both front tyres (red sidewall stripe) at the bottom corners, blue nose centre, antenna; long right-hand corner with red/white kerb and concrete wall + catch fence on the right, run-off and barriers on the left.
- Hard cut between 2.60 s and 3.04 s to Shot 2 (samples 7-23): cockpit camera with halo hoop and centre pillar, two mirrors, steering wheel held by two gloved hands. Wheel turned right around 3.9-4.8 s, near straight 5.2-7.0 s, then a large left lock (~80-90 deg) from ~7.8 s to the end. A dark rival car is ahead, small and central on the straight, then off to the left through the left corner.

## Inferred / modelled
- Ego path integrated analytically from keyframed speed and yaw-rate tables (deterministic lookup, absolute time); track centreline derived from the ego path minus a lateral racing-line offset. Cut placed at 2.82 s (between samples, not observed exactly).
- Track: road ribbon, edge lines, textured red/white kerbs (in-memory DataTexture), run-off areas, walls/boards, translucent catch fences with posts, instanced seeded trees, grandstands (box wedges, one with a canopy roof), overhead green gantry, video screen, light poles, crane, white buildings, fog-free distant mountain cones, vertex-coloured sky dome.
- Ego car: lofted chassis/nose, sidepods, front/rear wheels (front steer), front wing, suspension, halo, mirrors; steering wheel articulated (rotation from STEER keyframes) with gloves attached to the grips and forearms re-aimed each frame from hands to fixed elbows.
- Rival: box/cylinder proxy following the same racing line with a time lead (2.8 s -> 1.6 s) so it closes in under braking and appears to the left in the corner.
- Camera FOV ~60 deg vertical for both shots; positions/pitch chosen to match the pixel layout of the car parts.

## Feedback
None yet (initial submission). Speeds, yaw rates, the cut time, lighting levels and landmark positions are estimates to be checked against render feedback.

rounds.reason: Fix cockpit proxy layout (navy bodywork, dash cowl, flatter halo band, slimmer mirrors and forearms), move trees off run-off, relocate video screen, wider front track in nose cam.

## Remaining uncertainties
Exact speeds, yaw rates, FOV and the cut frame (2.82 s, between samples at 2.60 and 3.04 s) are inferred, not observed. Landmark positions are approximate, and trees are seeded proxies rather than matched individually. The rival car is a coarse dark proxy and looks somewhat smaller than in the reference on the straight. Cockpit parts are boxes (mirror pods are not rounded), and the steering-wheel buttons, logos, halo text and the watermark are left out on purpose at L1. Track elevation changes are only approximated through car-pitch keyframes. Motion between samples is analytic interpolation and was not checked frame by frame.
